questions.q: Prolapsed intervertebral disc (PIVD) is best described as:
opts: Protrusion of disc causing compression of spinal cord/nerve
questions.exp: PIVD: protrusion of disc → compression of spinal cord/nerves. (Book p181)
m/c disc to prolapse: L4-L5 > L5-S1. (Book p181)
Nucleus pulposus (NP): type II collagen; annulus fibrosus: type I. (Book p181)
Annulus fibrosus (AF): type I collagen. (Book p181)

questions.q: Mechanism of injury in PIVD includes:
questions.exp: Mechanism of injury: abnormal loading of spine and degeneration of spine. (Book p181)

questions.q: Other mechanism of injury leading to PIVD is:
questions.exp: Mechanism of injury: degeneration of spine. (Book p181)

questions.q: First stage in progression of disc degeneration is:
questions.exp: Progression of disc degeneration: Degeneration → Prolapse → Extrusion → Sequestration. (Book p181)

questions.q: 'Prolapse' stage in disc degeneration corresponds to:
questions.exp: Prolapse stage: bulging of nucleus pulposus. (Book p181)

opts: AF breaks and NP comes out
questions.exp: Extrusion: AF breaks and NP comes out. (Book p181)
Sequestration: extruded NP breaks away. (Book p181)
Causes of canal stenosis: PIVD and vertebral degeneration in OA. (Book p181)

questions.q: Vertebral degeneration in OA causes canal stenosis by:
questions.exp: Vertebral degeneration in OA → excessive growth of abnormal bone → stenosis. (Book p181)

questions.q: m/c site of canal stenosis is:
questions.exp: m/c site of canal stenosis: lumbar. (Book p181)

questions.q: Age at presentation in PIVD is typically:
questions.exp: PIVD: age at presentation young, onset acute (canal stenosis: elderly, chronic). (Book p181)

questions.q: Onset of disease in canal stenosis is typically:
questions.exp: Canal stenosis: elderly, chronic onset; PIVD: young, acute onset. (Book p181)
Far lateral PIVD: impinges exiting nerve roots. (Book p181)
Paracentral (m/c): impinges traversing nerve roots. (Book p181)

questions.q: m/c injured nerve in lumbar PIVD is:
questions.exp: m/c injured nerve: L5 (LMNL d/t nerve root involvement). (Book p181)

questions.q: History in presentation of PIVD typically includes:
questions.exp: Clinical features: H/o lifting heavy objects, low back ache, sciatica, neurological deficits. (Book p182)
m/c cause of sciatica: PIVD. (Book p182)

opts: Back pain radiating to lower limb
Burning pain in sole of foot
questions.exp: Sciatica: back pain radiating to lower limb. (Book p182)
Sciatica increases with flexion, sneezing, coughing and sitting for prolonged duration. (Book p182)

questions.q: SLRT is positive when hip cannot be flexed more than:
questions.exp: SLRT (Straight Leg Raising Test): positive when unable to flex hip >30-35°. (Book p182)

questions.q: SLRT becomes positive because raising the leg:
opts: Causes stretching of compressed nerve → produces pain
questions.exp: SLRT: causes stretching of compressed nerve → produces pain. (Book p182)
MRI (IOC) for PIVD. (Book p182)

questions.q: Neurological examination in PIVD is done to:
opts: Localize the lesion depending on nerve roots involved
questions.exp: Neurological examination: to localize the lesion depending on nerve roots involved. (Book p182)
C5 myotome: elbow flexion. (Book p182)
C6 myotome: wrist extension. (Book p182)
C7 myotome: elbow extension & wrist flexion. (Book p182)
C8 myotome: finger flexion. (Book p182)
T1 myotome: finger abduction. (Book p182)
L2 myotome: hip flexion/iliopsoas. (Book p182)
L3 myotome: knee extension/quadriceps. (Book p182)
L4 myotome: ankle dorsiflexors/tibialis anterior. (Book p182)
L5 myotome: toe extensors/extensor hallucis longus. (Book p182)
S1 myotome: ankle plantar flexors/gastrosoleus. (Book p182)
C5 reflex: biceps. (Book p182)
C6 reflex: supinator (brachioradialis). (Book p182)
C7 reflex: triceps. (Book p182)
L3, L4 reflex: knee (quadriceps). (Book p182)
S1 reflex: ankle (gastrosoleus). (Book p182)

questions.q: First conservative treatment of PIVD is:
opts: Rest in semi-fowler position (supine with 30-40° flexion of spine)
questions.exp: Treatment 1: rest in semi-fowler position (supine with 30-40° flexion of spine). (Book p182)

questions.q: Second conservative treatment of PIVD is:
questions.exp: Treatment 2: physiotherapy. (Book p182)
